concepts.title: Globe and Latitudes
concepts.definition: A globe is a spherical model of the Earth; latitudes are imaginary horizontal lines running east-west, parallel to the equator.
concepts.key_idea: Latitudes measure distance north or south of the equator and help locate places on Earth.
question_patterns: explain latitudes on a globe
describe the key features of latitudes on a globe
what are the main characteristics of latitudes on a globe
why is latitudes on a globe important
give examples of latitudes on a globe

solution_steps.explain: The equator is the 0 degree latitude line that divides Earth into northern and southern hemispheres.
Major latitudes include Tropic of Cancer (23.5N), Tropic of Capricorn (23.5S), Arctic Circle (66.5N) and Antarctic Circle (66.5S).
Latitudes are measured in degrees from 0 at the equator to 90 at the poles.

worked_examples.question: What is the equator and what is its latitude?
worked_examples.solution: The equator is the imaginary line at 0 degrees latitude dividing Earth into two hemispheres.

worked_examples.question: Name two important latitudes besides the equator.
worked_examples.solution: Tropic of Cancer at 23.5N and Tropic of Capricorn at 23.5S.
worked_examples.answer: Tropic of Cancer, Tropic of Capricorn

exercises.question: Define latitude and state its range.

concepts.title: Longitudes and Time Zones
concepts.definition: Longitudes are imaginary vertical lines running from pole to pole; they determine time zones.
concepts.key_idea: Longitudes measure distance east or west of the Prime Meridian and are used to calculate time differences.
question_patterns: explain longitudes and time zones
describe the key features of longitudes and time zones
what are the main characteristics of longitudes and time zones
why is longitudes and time zones important
give examples of longitudes and time zones

solution_steps.explain: The Prime Meridian at 0 degrees longitude passes through Greenwich, England.
Earth rotates 360 degrees in 24 hours, so 1 degree = 4 minutes of time difference.
Time zones are based on 15-degree intervals, each representing 1 hour.

worked_examples.question: If it is noon at Greenwich, what time is it at 90 degrees east?
worked_examples.solution: 90 degrees east means 90*4=360 minutes=6 hours ahead, so 6 PM.

worked_examples.question: What is the time difference between 30E and 30W?
worked_examples.solution: Total difference is 60 degrees, 60*4=240 minutes=4 hours.

exercises.question: Calculate the time at 45E when it is 10 AM at Greenwich.
Explain how longitudes help determine time.

concepts.title: Map Reading and Symbols
concepts.definition: A map is a representation of the Earth's surface or part of it on a flat surface using symbols.
concepts.key_idea: Maps use conventional symbols to represent features like roads, rivers, railways and buildings.
question_patterns: explain map symbols and reading
describe the key features of map symbols and reading
what are the main characteristics of map symbols and reading
why is map symbols and reading important
give examples of map symbols and reading

solution_steps.explain: A map has a title, scale, direction indicator (north arrow), and legend or key.
Symbols in the legend represent real features -- blue for water, black for roads, etc.
Use the scale to measure distances and the direction arrow to orient the map.

worked_examples.question: What are the main components of a map?
What does a blue line on a map usually represent?

exercises.question: List the four main components of a map.
Explain the purpose of a map legend.

concepts.title: Directions and Compass
concepts.definition: Directions are determined using a compass; cardinal directions are North, South, East, and West.
concepts.key_idea: A compass needle points to magnetic north, helping find all four cardinal and four intermediate directions.
question_patterns: explain directions and compass use
describe the key features of directions and compass use
what are the main characteristics of directions and compass use
why is directions and compass use important
give examples of directions and compass use

solution_steps.explain: North, South, East, and West are the four main directions.
Northeast, Northwest, Southeast, and Southwest are intermediate directions.
A compass needle always points north-south, helping orient oneself.

worked_examples.question: What direction is between North and East?

exercises.question: How does a compass help in finding directions?

concepts.title: Scale of a Map
concepts.definition: Scale is the ratio between distance on a map and actual distance on the ground.
concepts.key_idea: Map scale allows conversion between map distances and real-world distances.
question_patterns: explain map scale
describe the key features of map scale
what are the main characteristics of map scale
why is map scale important
give examples of map scale

solution_steps.explain: Scale may be stated as a ratio (1:100000), a statement (1 cm = 1 km), or a linear scale bar.
Use a ruler to measure the distance between two points on the map.
Multiply map distance by the scale factor.

worked_examples.question: On a map with scale 1 cm = 5 km, two cities are 4 cm apart. What is the actual distance?
A map scale is 1:100000. If two points are 3 cm apart on the map, what is the ground distance?

exercises.question: On a 1:50000 map, 2 cm represents how many km?
Explain three ways of expressing map scale.

concepts.title: Kinds of Maps
concepts.definition: Maps are classified as physical, political, and thematic based on the information they show.
concepts.key_idea: Different map types serve different purposes -- physical maps show natural features, political maps show boundaries, thematic maps show specific data.
question_patterns: explain types of maps
describe the key features of types of maps
what are the main characteristics of types of maps
why is types of maps important
give examples of types of maps

solution_steps.explain: Physical maps show natural features like mountains, rivers, and plains.
Political maps show boundaries of countries, states, and cities.
Thematic maps show specific information like rainfall, population, or crops.

worked_examples.question: Which type of map shows mountains and rivers?
What does a political map show?
worked_examples.solution: Boundaries of countries, states, and cities.

exercises.question: Name three types of maps and what each shows.
Give one example of a thematic map.

concepts.title: Hemispheres of Earth
concepts.definition: The Earth is divided into hemispheres by the equator (northern/southern) and the Prime Meridian (eastern/western).
concepts.key_idea: Hemispheres help divide Earth into halves for geographical study.
question_patterns: explain hemispheres of earth
describe the key features of hemispheres of earth
what are the main characteristics of hemispheres of earth
why is hemispheres of earth important
give examples of hemispheres of earth

solution_steps.explain: The equator divides Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
The Prime Meridian divides Earth into Eastern and Western Hemispheres.
India lies in the Northern and Eastern Hemispheres.

worked_examples.question: Which hemisphere does India lie in?
What divides Earth into northern and southern hemispheres?

exercises.question: Name the four hemispheres of Earth.
In which hemispheres does India lie?

concepts.title: Finding Locations Using Coordinates
concepts.definition: The exact location of any place on Earth can be found using its latitude and longitude coordinates.
concepts.key_idea: Latitude and longitude together form a grid that uniquely identifies any point on Earth.
question_patterns: explain finding locations using coordinates
describe the key features of finding locations using coordinates
what are the main characteristics of finding locations using coordinates
why is finding locations using coordinates important
give examples of finding locations using coordinates

solution_steps.explain: Read the latitude value (north or south of equator).
Read the longitude value (east or west of Prime Meridian).
Find the intersection of the latitude and longitude lines.

worked_examples.question: What are the coordinates of a place at 28N, 77E?
worked_examples.solution: Latitude 28 degrees North, Longitude 77 degrees East -- this is near New Delhi.

worked_examples.question: How do latitude and longitude together locate a place?
worked_examples.solution: They form a grid; the intersection of a latitude line and longitude line gives the exact position.
worked_examples.answer: Intersection of lat and lon lines

exercises.question: Find the approximate coordinates of your city.
Explain how coordinates help locate places.
